The chromosome-scale genome assemblies presented here provide a foundation for investigating the evolutionary history of the genus Hordeum. Chromosome-scale resolution enables us to investigate how structural variations have shaped genome evolution, particularly in disrupting chromosomal collinearity. Traditionally, grass genomes were thought to possess relatively stable chromosome structures58; however, our findings challenge this assumption. Extensive structural variations and chromosomal rearrangements have contributed substantially to genomic divergence, ultimately resulting in the near-complete loss of collinearity in proximal regions. These rearrangements not only mark evolutionary divergence but also provide insights into the processes underlying speciation within Hordeum. Structural variations accumulated at markedly different rates across chromosome regions. Whereas proximal regions exhibit high variability, distal regions evolve more slowly. This uneven evolutionary rate has preserved footprints of ancient hybridization events across the genus, offering a historical record of interspecific gene flow. These findings provide empirical evidence for ancient hybridization and genome fusion during Hordeum evolution and establish a framework for identifying compatible genomic segments in future interspecific breeding efforts.

Industry observers note that nevertheless, whether the large inversions identified in this study contribute to adaptive evolution, reproductive isolation or other phenotypic consequences remains unknown and warrants future functional investigation. Whole-genome MSAs enabled us to compare genome-wide conservation across Hordeum species. Compared with animal genomes, which often display strong interspecies conservation, plant genomes—especially within rapidly evolving genera such as Hordeum—undergo dynamic changes driven by short generation times and rapid transposon expansion. These processes fuel the ongoing remodelling of plant genomes, resulting in high variability even among closely related taxa. Despite this rapid evolution, many genes remain conserved, whereas regulatory elements exhibit considerable turnover. This contrast offers unique opportunities: lineage-specific regulatory innovation can be harnessed for crop improvement, while core gene functions are retained. For example, regulatory elements associated with vernalization responses were found to vary across Hordeum species, suggesting that novel regulatory variants could be introduced into cultivated barley to fine-tune flowering behaviour. Beyond expanding genomic resources for Hordeum, this work provides a framework for investigating structural genome evolution, reconstructing complex evolutionary histories and harnessing genetic and regulatory diversity for barley improvement.

Recent findings suggest that plant material was obtained from genebanks at Institut für Pflanzgenetik und Kulturpflanzenforschung (IPK) Gatersleben, the US Department of Agriculture and the Nordic Genetic Resource Center. Accession numbers are listed in Supplementary Table 1.

Recent findings suggest that plants were grown under greenhouse conditions and high molecular weight (HMW) DNA was isolated from young leaf tissue according to published protocols10,60. Construction of HiFi libraries and Circular Consensus Sequencing using the PacBio Sequel IIe instrument (Pacific Biosciences) were essentially as described previously19. HiFi sequencing was done at IPK Gatersleben, Genomics and Transcriptomics Laboratory, Heinrich Heine University, Berry Genomics Co., Novogene and the University of Wisconsin Biotechnology Center DNA Sequencing Facility.

Industry observers note that in situ Hi-C libraries were prepared from young seedlings according to the previously published protocol, using DpnII for the digestion of crosslinked chromatin. Libraries were prepared as described61. Samples were quantified62 and sequenced with standard protocols from Illumina using Illumina NovaSeq 6000 devices (Illumina) at IPK Gatersleben and Novogene.

According to recent reports, A clone of the same H. erectifolium individual plant that was sequenced using PacBio HiFi was used for the construction of the optical genome map (OGM). A total of 2.5 million nuclei, purified from young leaves by flow cytometry, were embedded in agarose miniplugs and treated with proteinase K, following the protocol of Šimková et al.63. A total of 525 ng of HMW DNA was directly labelled at DLE-1 recognition sites using the standard Bionano Prep Direct Label and Stain protocol (Bionano) and analysed on the Bionano Saphyr platform. The resulting dataset, comprising 1.5 Tb of single-molecule data with an N50 of 247 kb, provided approximately 341× coverage of the H. erectifolium genome. This dataset was used to generate a de novo OGM assembly using Bionano Solve software (v3.6.1_11162020) with the standard configuration file optArguments_nonhaplotype_noES_noCut_DLE1_saphyr.xml.

To improve the contiguity of the PacBio HiFi assembly, the automatic hybrid scaffold pipeline integrated in Bionano Solve was run using the OGM assembly. The default DLE-1 Hybrid Scaffold configuration file was applied with the ‘resolve conflict’ option for conflict resolution. Conflicts between the sequence assembly and the OGM were manually curated and the pipeline was subsequently re-run using a modified conflict_cut_status.txt file.

Plants were grown under greenhouse conditions and total RNA was isolated from different tissues and developmental stages (Supplementary Table 5) using the RNAeasy Plant Mini Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany) or with Trizol reagent (Invitrogen) according to the manufacturers’ protocols. RNA-seq was performed on replicated bulk sample representing a specific developmental stage or tissue type. RNA-seq of individual samples and PacBio IsoSeq of RNA pools was performed as described previously10. Library construction and sequencing on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 devices (Illumina RNA-seq) and PacBio Sequel IIe (instruments) was done at IPK Gatersleben, Biomarker Technologies (BMK), the Genomics and Transcriptomics Laboratory at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf, Kazusa DNA Research Institute or Berry Genomics. The PacBio IsoSeq sequencing data was processed with the isoseq3 (v3.8.2) pipeline (PacBio - IsoSeq3, 2018/2024). The ploy-A tails were trimmed and concatenated transcripts removed with refine -require-polya-min-polya-length 12 teloprime.fasta. To generate non-redundant transcripts, we mapped the full-length non-concatenated reads were mapped to the genome with pbmm2 (v1.10.0) align -preset ISOSEQ -sort -bam-index CSI and redundant transcripts collapsed with isoseq3 collapse -do-not-collapse-extra-5exons.

In a recent development, pacBio HiFi reads were assembled using hifiasm (v0.13-r308 or v0.15.5-r350 or v0.16.1-r375)64. Pseudomolecules were constructed with the TRITEX pipeline26,27, and chimeric contigs or orientation errors were corrected based on manual inspection of Hi-C contact matrices. For allotetraploid species, subgenomes were phased using a previously developed haplotype-resolved genome assembly strategy10. The origin of the subgenomes and their potential ancestral contributors were previously investigated in detail by Brassac et al.1 To classify subgenomes in the polyploid genome, Mash (v2.3)65 was used to calculate pairwise chromosomal similarities between polyploid chromosomes and candidate ancestral genomes. The resulting distance matrix was used to infer subgenome origin and relationships. In species with high heterozygosity or outcrossing (H. brevisubulatum and H. murinum BBC2017), Hi-C data were incorporated during hifiasm (v0.15.5-r350)64 assembly to collapse haplotypes and assemble a representative haploid genome. Except for H. erectifolium, whose primary contigs were first hybrid-scaffolded using a Bionano optical map, followed by pseudomolecule construction with Hi-C data and the TRITEX pipeline30. Chloroplast genomes were assembled following previously published protocols10. HiFi reads were aligned to the barley cv. Morex chloroplast genome (GenBank accession EF115541) using minimap2 (v2.24-r1122)66 with the parameters -ax map-hifi–secondary=no–sam-hit-only. Alignments with mapping quality <30 were discarded. Aligned reads were converted to FASTQ format using SAMtools (v1.16.1)67 and assembled with Canu (v2.1.1)68 in PacBio HiFi mode with genome sizes from 120 to 400 kb in 10-kb increments. Circular sequences were identified and trimmed using BEDTools (v2.30.0)69 and annotated with GeSeq70. Fully annotated assemblies were aligned to the Morex chloroplast genome using MUMmer4 (v4.0.0beta2)71, and start positions and orientations of the SSC region were adjusted to match the reference using seqkit (v0.9.1)72. k-mer frequencies were calculated using Jellyfish(v2.2.6)73 and analysed with findGSE(v1.94)74 to estimate genome characteristics. Assembly quality, including QV and k-mer completeness, was evaluated using Merqury(v1.3)75.

It has been revealed that we performed de novo structural gene prediction, confidence classification and functional annotation, following the protocol described in Mascher et al.28. As evidences we used RNA-seq and IsoSeq data as described under above and Poales-filtered protein sequences downloaded from UniProt76 (July 2023). An additional consolidation step was carried out using the liftoff77 tool. In brief, all predicted gene models from one species were lifted over to all other genomes. Using Mikado78, we selected the best mapped gene models and unified all gene predictions accordingly. We classified predicted proteins into high and low-confidence categories. High-confidence proteins had over 80% coverage and were complete, either with significant hits in UniMag or UniPoa but not PTREP (https://trep-db.uzh.ch). Low-confidence proteins were incomplete with hits in UniMag or UniPoa but not PTREP, or were complete without hits in any database.

We benchmarked the annotations with BUSCO (v5.8.0)79 (dataset: poales_odb12), OMARK (omamer verision 2.1.0/omark v0.3.1)80 and psauron (v1.0.6)81.

Sources indicate that orthogroups based on the primary protein sequences from 27 annotated Hordeum accessions were calculated using Orthofinder (v2.5.5)82. The scripts for the calculation of core, shell and cloud genes are deposited in the repository at https://github.com/PGSB-HMGU/BPGv2. Core genes contain at least 1 gene model from all 27 compared accessions. Shell genes contain gene models from at least 2 Hordeum accessions and at most 26. Genes clustered with genes only from the same genotype were defined as cloud genes. Annotations of H. vulgare Morex and H. bulbosum were not included during the consolidation step. Therefore, to counteract any potential over- or under-presentation of these two species in any of the core, shell or cloud categories, we aligned all cloud genes for H. vulgare cv. Morex and H. bulbosum back to all other genomes and corrected for any missing genes. Gene Ontology-term enrichments were conducted with goatools (v1.4.4)83. Gene-based collinearity plots were drawn with GENESPACE84.

The RGAugury (v2.2)85 pipeline was used to identify from our annotation and classify nucleotide-binding site (NB-ARC) domain-encoding genes into different subgroups, based on domain and motif structures: TNL contain TIR, NBS and LRR domains; CNL contain CC, NBS and LRR domains; RNL contain RPW8, NBS and LRR domains; RN contain RPW8 and NBS domains only; NL contain NBS and LRR domains but lack TIR, CC and RPW8; TN contain TIR and NBS domains only; CN contain CC and NBS domains only; and NBS-only genes contain only the NBS domain. TIR, NBS, LRR, CC and RPW8 refer to the Toll/Interleukin-1 Receptor-like, Nucleotide-Binding Site, Leucine-Rich Repeat, Coiled-Coil and Resistance to Powdery Mildew 8-like domains, respectively. An NLR gene cluster is defined based on the genomic proximity of NLR genes. Specifically, any two NLR genes located within 500 kb of each other are grouped into the same cluster by bedtools (v2.30.0)69. NLR genes were then grouped into clusters using bedtools (v2.30.0)69 merge with a maximum intergenic distance of 250 kb. Only clusters comprising no fewer than three NLR genes were retained. Pan-NLR analysis was performed based on orthogroups identified using OrthoFinder (v2.5.5)82 across all NLR genes. Core orthogroups are defined as orthogroups that contain at least one gene model from each of the compared Hordeum accessions. Shell orthogroups include gene models from at least two and at most 26Hordeum accessions. Gene models that were not assigned to any orthogroup (singletons) or were grouped only with genes from the same genotype were classified as cloud genes.

Recent findings suggest that open reading frames longer than 100 codons were searched for the presence of PPR and mTERF motifs using hmmsearch from the HMMER suite (http://hmmer.org) using hidden Markov models as defined in Cheng et al.86. for the PPR family and PF02536 from the Pfam 32.0 database (http://pfam.xfam.org)87 for the mTERF motif. Downstream processing of the hmmsearch results for the PPR proteins followed the pipeline described in Gutmann et al.88. The RfCTD domain recently identified as a unique feature of RFL-PPRs89 was included in the gene annotations. P-class and PLS-class genes with scores below 100 and 240, respectively, were excluded from the annotation as they are unlikely to represent functional PPR genes, as defined previously (IWGSC 2018)90.

The analyses described here used a number of tools from the toolkits vg (v1.61.0)91, odgi (v0.8.3-26-gbc7742ed)92, bcftools (v1.21)67 and seqkit (v2.9.0)72. All scripts used for graph construction and analysis are available at https://github.com/cropgeeks/panHordeum. Owing to computational limitations, we built an alignment of Hordeum whole genomes with Cactus47. We selected H. marinum BCC 2001 over H. marinum H559 on the basis of its higher assembly quality. Genome haplomes were soft-masked with bedtools69 using their respective repeat annotations. The guide tree required for the Cactus alignment was taken from the Orthofinder93 output generated as part of this study. Apart from setting appropriate resource parameters (that is, threads, memory and disk), we ran Cactus with default parameters. We transformed the resulting whole-genome alignment into a super-pangenome graph using hal2vg (https://github.com/ComparativeGenomicsToolkit/hal2vg), with the –noAncestors flag, and then further processed it with vg convert to get the final pangenome graph in GFA format (https://github.com/GFA-spec/GFA-spec). We computed basic graph statistics using odgi stats with the –summarize option, which included graph size, number of nodes, edges, paths and steps. To characterize the conservation of the different segments of the graph, we classified nodes as core, shell, or cloud. A node was considered ‘core’ if it was traversed by all samples’ paths, ‘cloud’ if it was traversed by a single sample’s path, and ‘shell’ otherwise. The same classification was done at the base level. Both computations were performed using the odgi toolkit (implementation details in class_stats.sh). To evaluate the agreement of haplotype sequences with their representation in the graph, we first extracted the linear sequences of all haplotypes as encoded in the graph using odgi paths with the –fasta option. These sequences were subsequently partitioned by source genome using seqkit grep, creating direct pairwise comparisons between input genomes and their graph-encoded counterparts. For each genome pair, we performed exact sequence matching, confirming whether each input sequence (or its reverse complement) was precisely preserved in the graph-encoded version (implementation details available in script fidelity.py). We computed pangenome graph growth curves based on the full graph using odgi heaps with 100 permutations of the input genomes. Results were plotted using script heaps_fit.R distributed with the odgi toolkit92. Whole-graph analysis turned out to be computationally prohibitive (job runtime limits and/or memory requirements) for several of the required tools from the vg and odgi toolkits, given a graph of this size and complexity. We therefore extracted subgraphs equating to individual chromosome paths for H. vulgare cv. Morex, which we used as the basis for all variant analyses. We used vg chunk for subgraph extraction. Variants were called from the chromosome-level subgraphs directly, using vg deconstruct. This generated VCF output containing the full range of variant sizes. To prepare structural variants from the graph for further analysis we broadly followed the variant decomposition approach used by the Human Pangenome Consortium94. This involved the removal of top-level variants of length >100,000 bp with vcfbub (https://github.com/pangenome/vcfbub), realigning alternate alleles against the reference for each variant using vcfwave (vcflib v1.0.2)95, and finally normalizing the resulting variants with bcftools norm67. We then added variant length information (SVLEN) to the VCF files with a custom script to allow extraction of structural variants based on the length difference between reference and alternate allele (>50 bp) and classified structural variations as deletions or insertions based on the directionality of the difference (insertion: string length REF  string length ALT). The resulting VCF files were converted to BED format with bcftools query. Variant density plots were computed with custom R scripts using ggplot2 (v3.5.1)96. To explore the possibility of using the graph for read mapping and genotyping, we attempted to index the graph using vg gbwt/vg index/vg minimizer. This turned out to be computationally prohibitive in terms of job runtime limits on two separate compute facilities used, and thus we were unable to use the graph for the valuation of read mapping. We conducted graph-based conservation analysis with Pansel97, a tool used for calculation of diversity/conservation metrics directly from pan-genome graphs. The default bin size of 1kbp was used, along with all other parameters on default settings. Results were plotted using ggplot2 (v3.5.1)96.

Single-copy genes were identified using BUSCO (v5.4.6)79 in B. distachyon (v3.0)98, O. sativa (IRGSP-1.0)99, S. bicolor (NCBIv3)99, T. monococcum100, H. vulgare FT11 (ref. 19) and the 29 Hordeum haplomes collected in this study. Protein sequences of BUSCO single-copy genes present in all 34 haplomes were concatenated and aligned using MAFFT (v7.490)101. Well-aligned regions were filtered using Gblocks (v0.91b)102 with parameters -t=extractedp -b4 = 5 -b5=h. A maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree was then constructed using RAxML (v8.2.12)103 with the PROTGAMMAWAG substitution model and the rapid bootstrap algorithm with 100 replicates. To facilitate genome-wide alignment, all 34 haplomes were masked using RepeatMasker (v4.1.1; http://www.repeatmasker.org) with a pan-genome TE library generated by panEDTA. The masked genomes and the inferred species tree were then used as input for Cactus (v2.6.5)47 to generate whole-genome MSAs. The loss rate of genomic elements was defined as the size of the reconstructed ancestral sequence at the corresponding genomic position in the multiple genome alignment.

It has been revealed that to precisely construct phylogenetic trees and estimate divergence times within the genus Hordeum, we included four additional outgroup genomes: B. distachyon (v3.0)98, O. sativa (IRGSP-1.0)99, S. bicolor (NCBIv3)104 (all downloaded from Ensembl Plants; https://plants.ensembl.org/index.html) and T. monococcum100 (https://wheat.pw.usda.gov/GG3/pangenome). We constructed phylogenetic trees using four approaches. The first two methods were based on whole-genome single-copy genes. Orthologous genes were identified from the genomes of our 34 Hordeum haplomes and four outgroup genomes using OrthoFinder (v2.5.5)82, yielding 2,198 single-copy genes. For the concatenation-based approach, the CDS sequences of these genes were concatenated and aligned with MAFFT (v7.490)101, and well-aligned regions were retained using Gblocks (v0.91b)102 with the parameters -t=extractedp, -b4 = 5, -b5=h; phylogenetic inference was then performed in IQ-TREE (v2.2.2.6)105. For the coalescence-based approach, the CDS sequences of each single-copy gene were aligned separately using MAFFT (v7.490)101, high-quality regions were selected with Gblocks (v0.91b)102 using the same parameters, individual gene trees were reconstructed with IQ-TREE (v2.2.2.6)105, and a species tree was inferred from these gene trees using ASTRAL-Pro3 (CASTLES-Pro, v1.23.3.6)106. The remaining two methods were based on whole-genome MSAs generated with Cactus. In the CASTER-pair (CASTLES-Pro, v1.23.3.6)107 approach, the whole-genome MSA was used to infer a phylogenetic tree rooted with S. bicolor, while in the CASTER-site (CASTLES-Pro, v1.23.3.6)107 approach, the whole-genome MSA was analysed similarly but using site-based inference, also rooted with S. bicolor.

According to recent reports, to estimate divergence times, genomic regions showing strong phylogenetic discordance (nRF > 0.21) were first excluded based on the genome-wide discordance analysis. 4DTV sites were extracted from MSAs of single-copy genes. Divergence times between barley and outgroup species were obtained from the TimeTree database (https://timetree.org/)108. Finally, species divergence times within the genus Hordeum were estimated using the MCMCtree program in PAML (v4.4)109.

It has been revealed that we excluded multiple haplomes from the same species and retained a final set of 32 Hordeum haplomes for comparative analysis. All haplomes pairs were aligned against each other using minimap2 (v2.24-r1122)66 with the parameters -2 -K 5 G -f 0.005 -x asm10, and the resulting alignments were stored in PAF format for visualization via dot plots. For each reference haplomes, we calculated the alignment coverage in non-overlapping 5 Mb windows, considering only alignments with a mapping quality greater than 20. Coverage values were normalized across the haplomes by the average coverage to produce normalized coverage profiles. In species that diverged more than 9 Ma, a bimodal distribution of normalized coverage was observed, allowing a threshold of 0.5 to distinguish distal and proximal regions (Extended Data Fig. 3b,c). Finally, genome-wide alignment and normalized coverage profiles were used to manually define the size and boundaries of proximal and distal regions across all species. Reverse-orientation alignments were extracted as indicators of putative inversion events. Two metrics were calculated for each pairwise comparison: (1) the number of reverse-orientation alignments per Mb and (2) the proportion of bases covered by reverse-orientation alignments. These metrics were separately calculated for proximal and distal chromosomal regions to compare the rates of inversion accumulation during species divergence. Linear regression models including divergence time, chromosomal region type (proximal or distal) and their interaction term were used to evaluate differences in the accumulation rates of reverse-orientation alignments between regions.

According to recent reports, all other Hordeum genomes were aligned to the MorexV3 (ref. 28) reference genome using wfmash (v0.9.1-3; https://github.com/waveygang/wfmash) with the parameters -p 90 -l 0. Inversions were then identified using SyRI (v1.5.5)110 with parameters -F P -f–nosnp. Only inversions larger than 2 Mb and located outside of the proximal regions were retained for further analysis.

Based on the 2,198 single-copy orthologues identified in the section ‘Phylogeny and divergence time estimation’ and using the genome-wide concatenated single-copy gene tree as a reference, we conducted sliding-window gene tree analyses (Extended Data Fig. 6a). All single-copy genes were grouped into non-overlapping windows of 25 genes with a step size of 2 genes. Within each window, protein sequences were aligned using MAFFT (v7.490)101, and well-aligned regions were retained using Gblocks (v0.91b)102 with the parameters -t=extractedp -b4 = 5 -b5=h. Local window trees were built with FastTree (v2.1.11)111 (default GTR + CAT, 20 rate categories), starting from neighbour-joining trees and optimized with minimum-evolution and nearest-neighbour interchange moves; branch support was calculated using Shimodaira–Hasegawa-like values. Each resulting tree was rooted with S. bicolor as the outgroup using ETE3 (v3.1.2)112, and the nRF distance was calculated against the reference tree using the parameter –min_support_src 90. The nRF metric quantifies topological dissimilarity between trees, with values ranging from 0 (identical topology) to 1 (completely different topologies). Based on the nRF distribution, we identified 0.21 as a threshold to separate background from discordant signal peaks (Extended Data Fig. 6b). To evaluate the robustness of discordant region detection, we repeated the sliding-window analyses using alternative parameter settings (30 genes with step sizes of 1 and 5 genes). The major discordance peaks were consistently recovered across different window sizes and step lengths, indicating that peak detection was not sensitive to parameter selection (Supplementary Fig. 52). Genomic regions containing at least 10 overlap windows with nRF ≥ 0.21 were defined as candidate introgressed regions. For each candidate region, we reconstructed local phylogenetic trees using the same procedure as for the genome-wide tree. The topological comparison of these local trees with the reference tree enabled the inference of introgression origins. The AU test113 implemented in IQ-TREE (v2.2.2.6)105, was used to compare local reference trees and local phylogenetic trees. A P value (p-AU) lower than 0.05 indicated that the tree was significantly rejected.

Genomes of 20 diploid Hordeum species were searched for potential HGT genes from grasses of the subfamily Panicoideae. Regions of interest were identified in the genomes using BLAST (v2.12.0+)114 against four potential donor species: Panicum hallii (v3.2), Setaria italica (v2.2), Paspalum vaginatum (v3.1) and Paspalum notatum (GCA_036689595.1) (Supplementary Table 10). BLAST results were filtered to retain hits with a sequence identity of ≥95% and an alignment length of ≥150 bp. The same process was applied to H. vulgare cv. Morex (v3), which served as a negative control. H. vulgare is widely recognized as a species that lacks HGT genes from the Panicoideae subfamily39,41,42. Hits from potential donors that were found in both the Hordeum recipient genomes and H. vulgare were excluded from further analysis. This filtering was conducted using the intersect tool from BEDTools (v2.26.0)69, with an overlap threshold of 20%. Finally, the identified regions were compared with newly available annotations, and corresponding candidate genes were extracted. In this step, we identified 5,169 candidate genes.

According to recent reports, to verify the foreign (that is, Panicoideae) origin of the candidate HGT genes identified as described above, phylogenetic trees were constructed for each candidate. Homologues were retrieved from a set of representative Poaceae species and two outgroups (Ananas comosus and Musa acuminata) (Supplementary Table 10) using BLASTn (e-value cutoff of 10−10). The retrieved sequences were aligned with the Hordeum HGT gene candidates using MUSCLE (v3.8)115. The alignments were trimmed using trimAl (v1.2) with an automated trimming method116. Phylogenetic trees were constructed using PhyML (v3.1)117, with 1,000 bootstrap iterations and the GTR substitution model. The resulting trees were reviewed semi-automatically with the assistance of the Newick Utilities suite118. A candidate gene was considered a true HGT gene if the gene sequence was nested within the PACMAD clade. TE-related genes were filtered out and only high-confidence, protein-coding genes were retained for further analysis. Out of 5,169 candidate genes, 4,393 did not pass through the primary phylogenetic validation and 776 genes remained. Candidate genes that passed the first step of verification were cross-referenced with orthogroups previously created during pan-genome construction. For groups containing more than one candidate gene, a consensus sequence was generated using MAFFT (v7.520)102 for MSA, followed by the cons tool from EMBOSS (v6.5.7.0)119 to produce the consensus. These consensus sequences were subsequently used for BLASTn searches. Hits from at least five species, including minimally one from Panicoideae, were required for tree construction. Phylogenetic trees were then constructed as described above, using MAFFT as the aligner. Alignments and trees were reviewed manually: orthogroups supporting the HGT scenario were retained, and genes in these groups were classified as either foreign or native, based on their position on the tree. The neighbour of transferred genes was marked as presumed donor if the branch represented one genus or species, otherwise the donor was marked as unknown. The entire orthogroup was considered to have a native copy if it contained at least one gene marked ‘native’, regardless of which species that gene was present in.

To determine the transfer times of genes during the evolutionary history of the lineage, an ancestral state reconstruction was conducted for each gene independently. The marginal ancestral state was inferred using the equal rate model120, applying the maximum-likelihood approach described by Pagel121 and implemented in the phytools package122. To ensure accuracy, the results were verified and adjusted for cases where genes were found in multiple tips but not in their common ancestor. In such instances, the presence of the gene was manually introduced at the ancestor node. For each node in the phylogenetic tree, both the originally reconstructed values and the manually adjusted values were visualized.

According to recent reports, genes from all orthogroups were annotated using eggNOG-mapper web server (v2.1.12)123,124. Gene Ontology terms were extracted for each group and enrichment analysis was performed using the clusterProfiler package (v4.14.3), with a significance threshold of an adjusted P value of 0.05 (ref. 125).

According to recent reports, RNA-seq data for inflorescence, leaf and root tissues previously generated for 19 Hordeum species were used in this study (RNA-seq data for H. bulbosum were not available). Read trimming on quality (Q30) and removal of sequencing adapters were done using Trimmomatic (v0.32)126. Cleaned reads from each library were then mapped to the corresponding reference genome using the STAR aligner (v2.7.7a)127. Quantification of mapped reads was done using the subread package v1.5.2 with featureCounts (v2.0.1)128 followed by normalization using the trimmed mean of M-values (TMM) method implemented in the edgeR package (v4.2.1)129. Genes were considered to be expressed if TMM ≥ 1 in at least one tissue.

Recent findings suggest that structurally intact and fragmented TEs were annotated for each genome using the panEDTA (v0.1) pipeline31. In addition to the curated TREP database (https://trep-db.uzh.ch/)130, TE classification followed the EDTA ontology (https://github.com/oushujun/EDTA/blob/master/bin/TE_Sequence_Ontology.txt), with manual curation of TE categories. High-confidence gene models from H. vulgare cv. MorexV3 was supplied via the -cds parameter to exclude genic sequences from TE annotation. For each genome, the length, classification, insertion time and divergence metrics of intact LTR retrotransposons were extracted from the intact.gff3 and pass.list output files. To investigate TE family expansion and intergenomic relationships, we used the TEpop framework (https://github.com/wicker314/TEpop) to treat each TE as an individual sample for population structure analysis46. PCA was then performed using FlashPCA2 (ref. 131) to explore the major patterns of TE variation across Hordeum species. To infer the formation time of tetraploid genomes from TE bursts, full-length LTR/Copia elements were extracted from tetraploid assemblies and clustered using CD-HIT (v4.8.1)132 with the parameters -n 5 -c 0.9 -d 0 -aL 0.9 -aS 0.9 -g 1 based on sequence similarity. To avoid potential bias caused by large-scale segmental exchanges between subgenomes, genomic regions identified as exchanged segments were excluded from this analysis (Supplementary Table 13). TEs that were shared between polyploid subgenomes but absent from their corresponding diploid progenitors were defined as post-allopolyploidization insertions. The insertion time distributions of these elements were used to reconstruct TE dynamics after subgenome fusion, and the onset of the insertion peak was used to estimate the timing of polyploid genome formation.

To identify conserved elements across Hordeum genomes, outgroup species were removed from the HAL alignment file using halRemoveGenome in Cactus (v2.6.5). Genome-wide MSAs were then extracted in MAF format using cactus-hal2maf with the parameters “–chunkSize 1000000–noAncestors–onlyOrthologs–noDupes”, using MorexV3 as the reference genome. Alignment blocks containing fewer than 10 sequences were filtered out in MSAs. A neutral model of evolution was fitted to the Hordeum phylogeny using fourfold degenerate sites from chromosome 3H of barley, using phyloFit from the PHAST package (v1.4)133. Based on the genome-wide multiple alignments and the trained neutral model, conserved elements were identified using PhastCons with the “–most-conserved” flag. The conserved and non-conserved models were trained with a target genome coverage of 0.45, and the expected length of conserved elements was set to 8 bp.

Industry observers note that ATAC–seq libraries were prepared from fresh leaf tissue at 3–5 leaf stage. Nuclei were isolated by fine chopping the tissue in isolation buffer (0.25 M sucrose, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 10 mM MgCl2, 1% Trion X-100, 5 mM β-Mercaptoethanol) supplemented with 1× Halt Protease Inhibitor Cocktail (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Following isolation, nuclei were quantified via flow cytometry and 75,000 nuclei were subjected to tagmentation using the Tagment DNA Enzyme (TDE1, Illumina) at 37 °C for 30 min. Transposed DNA was purified using the MinElute PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen), libraries were amplified with NEBNext High-Fidelity 2x PCR Master Mix (Newly introduced England Biolabs), and the final library purification was performed using VAHTSTM DNA Clean Beads (Vazyme) according to standard protocols from the manufacturers. Libraries were quantified as described previously62 and sequenced (paired-end, 2× 151 cycles, Illumina NovaSeq 6000, IPK Gatersleben) following protocols provided by the manufacturer (Illumina).

Adapter trimming and quality filtering were performed using Trim Galore (v0.6.4_dev; https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore.git) with the following parameters: -q 25–phred33–stringency 3–length 60–paired -j 10. Only read pairs with both ends retained were used in subsequent analyses. Trimmed reads were aligned to the reference genome using BWA (v0.7.17)134. The resulting SAM files were converted to BAM format and sorted using SAMtools (v1.10)67. Only properly paired reads with mapping quality ≥ 30 were retained (-f 2 -F 1804 -q 30), and further sorted by read name to enable mate information correction using samtools fixmate. Duplicate reads were marked using Picard MarkDuplicates (v2.21.9, https://broadinstitute.github.io/picard/) with VALIDATION_STRINGENCY=LENIENT and REMOVE_DUPLICATES=false. After marking, only properly paired, non-duplicate reads were retained and re-sorted by coordinate to produce final cleaned BAM files for downstream analysis. BAM indices were generated using samtools index. Peaks were called using MACS2 (v2.2.9.1)135. The effective genome size (-g) was set to 4.2 Gb, approximating the size of the barley genome. Peaks were called with automatic threshold evaluation (–cutoff-analysis), and all duplicate reads were retained during the analysis to preserve biological signal.

VRN1 and ZCCT genes were identified in all assembled wild barley genomes using blastn searches (blast-plus/2.12.0)114 with VRN1 MorexV3 (NC_058522.1:c528157887–528147799) and NCBI GenBank ZCCTa/b/c queries (AY485977, AY485978 and AY687931). Corresponding regions were extracted from genome assemblies by bedtools (v2.26.0)69 and manually annotated and analysed by Geneious Prime software (v2024.0.5; https://www.geneious.com). Sequence similarity visualization of the 2 kb region upstream of the transcription start site and the first intron of VRN1 genes was done by flexidot (v1.06)136. The 79-bp deletion in H. cordobense and H. muticum VRN1 gene was detected by MSA of the extracted VRN1 sequences from wild Hordeum species and winter cultivar Igri in Geneious Prime software (v2023.0.4; https://www.geneious.com) with MAFFT101. The critical region of cultivar Igri was identified in a previous study51.

It has been revealed that three biological replicates were analysed for each stage (14 DAG, 28 DAG) of H. cordobense and H. californicum grown under controlled non-vernalizing conditions (21 °C day:18 °C night, 14 h light:10 h dark photoperiod). Total RNA was extracted from frozen leaf tissue using a Quick-RNA Miniprep Kit (Zymo Research). RNA quality and concentration were evaluated with a Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies) on RNA 6000 Nano chips (Agilent Technologies). H. cordobense 28 DAG RNA-seq libraries and small RNA-seq libraries were constructed according to Illumina instructions and sequenced on a NovaSeq 6000 platform at Novogene. Other sequencing libraries (H. cordobense 14 DAG and H. californicum 14 and 28 DAG; small RNA and RNA-seq) were constructed at the Institute of Experimental Botany (Olomouc) using NEBNext Multiplex Small RNA Library Prep Set for Illumina and NEBNext Ultra RNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina with poly-A selection and sequenced on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform, 150 PE mode.

Small RNA-seq read trimming and sequencing adaptor removal were done with cutadapt (v3.4)137. Only reads of length 21–24 nt were used for subsequent analyses. ShortStack (v4)138 was used to map small RNA reads to the corresponding genome with default parameters. Bigwig files were created from bam files in a combination of samtools (v1.11)67 and deepTools (v3.5.6)139 with parameters bigwigAverage, bamCoverage–binSize 10,–normalizeUsing BPM. Visualization of small RNA and mRNA bigwig files were done with pyGenomeTracks (v3.9)140.

It has been revealed that RNA-seq read trimming on quality (Q30) and sequencing adaptor removal were done with Trimmomatic (v0.32)126. Resulting high-quality reads from each library were mapped onto the corresponding reference genome using STAR (v2.7.7a)127, with default parameters. Mapped reads quantification was done by rsem (v1.3.3)141.

Ten seeds per each of 14 selected Hordeum species accessions (BCC 2067 H. cordobense, BCC 2058 H. californicum, BCC 2014 H. muticum, BCC 2055 H. jubatum, BCC 2001 H. marinum, BCC 2009 H. murinum subsp. murinum, BCC 2017 H. murinum subsp. glaucum, BCC 2023 H. flexuosum, BCC 2026 H. erectifolium, BCC 2028 H. pubiflorum, BCC 2043 H. pusillum, BCC 2059 H. intercedens, BCC 2065 H. patagonicum and BCC 2069 H. roshevitzii) were used. Spring cultivated barley genotypes Morex and Golden Promise and winter genotypes Igri and Antonella were included as controls and were treated identically to wild species. Seeds were stratified at 4 °C for 4 days, germinated in Petri dishes on moist filter paper and then transferred to soil. Plants were grown under controlled non-vernalizing conditions (21 °C day:18 °C night, 14 h light:10 h dark photoperiod) in a growth chamber and cultivated until senescence. Days to flowering were scored in three-day intervals, and the plants were considered flowering at the first emergence of the awn tips. Plants were imaged using a Nikon D5600 digital camera.

Industry observers note that the elongated outer glume 1 (eog1) mutants from cultivated barley59, including eog1.a (GSHO 1891), eog1.c (GSHO 1892), eog1.e (GSHO 285) and macrolepis (lep-e.1; GSHO 960), were obtained from the Barley Genetic Stock Collection. Several mutants, namely M2342, M9630, M9815 and M11405, were identified from independent M2 lines of the previously established barley HTX mutagenesis population142. SEM observations were conducted using a Hitachi SEM SU8081 following a standard protocol143. Young inflorescences were sampled and examined. Allelism test was performed by crossing M9630 with GSHO 1891 and GSHO 1892, respectively. All F1 progeny exhibited elongated glumes on the central fertile spikelet (Extended Data Fig. 12d). Sequence-specific amplification of the C2H2-zinc-finger transcription factor gene was performed using primers T-70820-F (5′-TAGGACCGCATATTTCCAGG-3′) and T-70820-R (5′-GAACAGTTCCAAGGCGAAAG-3′). The resulting amplicons were sequenced using Sanger sequencing.

Industry observers note that clean reads (Supplementary Table 20) were obtained by removing the adapters, reads containing N bases and low-quality reads using fastp (v0.20.1) with default parameters144. Clean reads were mapped to their respective reference genomes via Hisat2 v2.1.0 with default parameters145. Read counts were determined from the mapping files via featureCounts (v2.0.1) using standard parameters128, and the TPM values of each gene were calculated. Spike-specific expressed genes were defined as having less than 5% TPM in other tissues146. The heatmap was generated using the pheatmap R package (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pheatmap) based on the normalized TPM values. Venn diagrams were drawn using the eulerr package (v6.1.0; https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=eulerr). A local BLAST search was performed using the deduced amino acids of HORVU.MOREX.r3.2HG0170820.1 (EOG1) as the query against the 24 Hordeum genome sequences to identify homologous proteins. Amino acid sequence alignment was carried out using MUSCLE (v3.8)115, and the resulting MSA was visualized with the Simple MSA Viewer function of TBtools II147.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan and Juventus are both keeping tabs on Benjamin Sesko’s situation at Manchester United, according to a report.

According to recent reports, united paid around €80m to sign Sesko from RB Leipzig, hoping he would be the long-term fix for the No.9 position. Last season he performed reasonably well, scoring 11 goals in 30 Premier League games which was not bad for a 22-year-old in a new league.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This season, however, he is stuck on one goal in four league games, having spent time out injured too. With major changes at Old Trafford – including the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino as the head coach – it is another blank slate for the squad.

Sources indicate that for example, club captain Bruno Fernandes has been linked with a move to Milan. Now, according to journalist Alessandro Jacobone, a fresh idea has emerged for the centre-forward position, perhaps if the pursuit of Nicolo Tresoldi does not go to proposal.

“Juve and Milan are keeping an eye on things. But summer is the most realistic scenario. Benjamin Šeško could leave Manchester United, with Juventus and Milan having already made some preliminary enquiries to assess the financial feasibility of a potential move,” he remarked.

“For now, these are only preliminary discussions, useful for finding out the figures, conditions and possible deal structures. No concrete negotiations have been initiated.

Industry observers note that “Sources close to the player’s camp are also playing down the possibility of a transfer as early as January, making a potential move in the next summer window considerably more likely. One to watch.”.

According to recent reports, four of those 11 goals in his debut campaign came off the bench too as he developed a knack for being an impact substitute. This could give Milan food for thought, given they are looking for an alter-ego to Goncalo Ramos rather than someone to solely take over the striker role.

  • Bruno Fernandes will be bidding to inspire Manchester United to a huge victory when the Red Devils head to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:12.

Bruno Fernandes will be bidding to inspire Manchester United to a huge victory when the Red Devils head to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

The match will mark Mauricio Pochettino's first fixture in charge of the 20-time English champions, and he will be hoping for inspiration from his captain.

Fernandes has found it difficult to show his best form for the Red Devils this season, but the 32-year-old has still managed to come up with six goals and three assists in 14 appearances.

Here, Sports Mole looks at how the Portugal international has performed against Liverpool during his professional career.

Fernandes has faced Liverpool on 13 previous occasions during his professional career, boasting a record of five wins, three draws and five defeats.

The attacker has scored three times against the Reds, in addition to contributing two assists.

Eleven of Fernandes' appearances against Liverpool have come in the Premier League, boasting a record of three wins, three draws and five defeats, scoring twice and registering two assists.

Fernandes has also faced Liverpool twice in the FA Cup, helping Man United to record a 3-2 win in the fourth round of the competition in 2021, finding the back of the net, before playing in a 4-3 success for the Red Devils in the quarter-finals in March 2024.

The Portuguese's two Premier League goals against Liverpool have been at Old Trafford, so he would create some personal history by finding the back of the net at Anfield on Sunday.

Last season, Fernandes provided an assist in a 2-1 Man United win at Anfield, before helping the Red Devils record a 3-2 victory in the reverse game at Old Trafford.

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

Industry observers note that 'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'.

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness.

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list.

According to recent reports, joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an vital part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

It has been revealed that post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences.

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

It has been revealed that however, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

According to recent reports, called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

There were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010).

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Industry observers note that eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

In a recent development, storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

  • TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

Recent findings suggest that england always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

In a recent development, will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the substantial delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

It has been revealed that “I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

Sources indicate that A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

It has been revealed that “Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel mentioned. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL.

Recent findings suggest that england had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold mentioned later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”.

According to recent reports, two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”.

According to recent reports, kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

Industry observers note that “If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel mentioned when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against Upcoming Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

Industry observers note that “I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

It has been revealed that “But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”.

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

According to recent reports, trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel stated.

Recent findings suggest that “He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, noted the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango remarked at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Recent findings suggest that miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

According to recent reports, santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

Industry observers note that given England are ranked 45 places higher, their results, if not all performances, at the World Cup were commendable and the way in which they rattled Spain and should really have given themselves a bulwark against the comeback by converting their penalty at 2-1 up,  an away win should be relatively straightforward. But they did lose on their last visit to Prague in a Euro 2020 qualifier having won 5-0 in the home leg.

Inter president Giuseppe Marotta has suggested that foreign ownership is key when it comes to modernising Italian clubs.

Last month, just before Milan’s resounding 3-1 derby win over Inter at San Siro, the two clubs unveiled the Generali Stadium. The vision is that it will become the upcoming home for the two sides within four years, replacing San Siro which recently turned 100 years old.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, it is not just about having a upcoming stadium for the sake of it, but rather to improve the fan experience and of course unlock commercial revenues that the current one cannot. It is one of many major aims Gerry Cardinale has to bring the Rossoneri back to the top of European football.

According to recent reports, beppe Marotta featured in the first episode of ‘L’impresa sportiva’, a segment on Il Sole 24 ORE’s TV program dedicated to the world of sport. He spoke about foreign ownership in Italy and the new stadium project, with his words via MilanPress.

“Football is a powerfully unifying phenomenon. After religion, I believe only sport can unite people by breaking down barriers. However, it’s also become a business. There are 12 foreign owners out of 20 in Serie A,” he began.

Recent findings suggest that “On the one hand, there’s a decline, on the other, we have to ask ourselves what would have happened to football in Italy without these foreign owners. It’s no coincidence that the future stadium is a joint venture between the two Milan clubs, both of which have American owners with, frankly, very farsighted vision.

ℹ️ The capacity, the slope, the sound retention, the LED membrane and more.

England should be seen as the favourites to win the UEFA Nations League ahead of the quarter-final draw, a former Three Lions striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Thomas Tuchel's side will learn their knockout fate on Friday morning when the draw for the last eight is held, and England head into the ceremony as one of the four seeded teams courtesy of finishing first in League A Group 3.

The Three Lions unexpectedly pipped world and European champions Spain to top spot courtesy of an engrossing 3-2 win over La Roja on Sunday, ending an unparalleled 43-game unbeaten run for Luis de la Fuente's side.

England will meet one of Belgium, Netherlands or Norway in the quarter-finals, while France, Portugal and Germany represent the other three Group A winners going for glory.

Despite the strength of the draw, former England striker Mark Hateley believes that Tuchel's men have made themselves the favourites to win the trophy for the first time, and also reserved special praise foe the goalkeeping heroics of James Trafford.

Recent findings suggest that asked if England are leading the charge for Nations League stardom, Hateley replied: "100%. That's the best I've seen England, or any team, play over a period of, say, 60 minutes.

"They were incredible: high press, press, press, press, going man for man, confident enough to go man for man at the back against the world champions, allowing your midfield players to jump up with the strikers.

“It was tremendous to watch, the very best we've seen from an England side for many, many years, honestly. It was superb. We went to 3-0, rightly so, and Spain never had a shot. Their first was 50 minutes in, in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that “Trafford must have thought 'this was a goddamn easy game.' The only time I think he was at fault was his starting position for the penalty, when Anderson brought the boy down. If his starting position had been higher, I think he'd have made the interception. That would be my only fault for the goalkeeper.

“If you’re a shot stopper, you’re a shot stopper - it’s just the other side of his game, where you're reading it and where you should be, playing as that sweeper.

"With the way we were pressing, the only ball really on for Spain was a ball in behind into the last third, which was empty for long periods. There was nobody there where I thought he could have been. But those are the things you pick up on and learn from.”.

England have only ever competed in the Nations League knockout stages once before in the inaugural 2018-19 edition, when they reached the finals courtesy of beating Spain and Croatia to first place in their group.

However, at a time when the Nations League Finals only comprised four teams, Gareth Southgate's side fell to a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands in the semi-finals, meaning that they are still awaiting their first knockout-phase win in the tournament.

England could only place third in the group stage of the 2020-21 tournament, before an embarrassing relegation to League B in the 2022-23 edition, although they swiftly returned to the top tier.

In the current format, England's record of five wins, one loss and 19 goals scored represented their best-ever performance in the group stage of the Nations League, fuelling the belief that the Three Lions can finally end their trophy drought in 2027.

Aiming to pick up where they left off before the break, Bologna will host Serie A's bottom side when Udinese visit Stadio Dall'Ara on Sunday.

After a sticky start, both clubs have already changed coaches, and the Rossoblu's new boss has sparked a surge up the standings.

Since Raffaele Palladino's arrival midway through September, Bologna have been a team transformed, winning five games from six and climbing towards the European places.

The Emilian club signed off for the international break with a run of four consecutive wins, with the highlight being a 4-2 victory over AC Milan at San Siro.

Last time out, the Rossoblu's revival continued in the Derby dell'Emilia against Parma, as their hosts were swiftly reduced to 10 men and ultimately suffered a 2-1 defeat.

So, having won none of their first five games during the short-lived Domenico Tedesco era, Bologna are now one of Serie A's form sides.

However, Palladino must still work on their awful home record, which stretches back through most of last season; so far this term, they have claimed five points from a possible 15 at the Dall'Ara.

Either home or away, Udinese have picked up just one from their last nine matches and are therefore stuck at the foot of the table.

The Bianconeri have put a meagre five points on the board so far, slumping into an unexpected crisis.

Safe mid-table finishers in back-to-back seasons under Kosta Runjaic, this campaign has completely unravelled, and even a change of coach has yet to produce results.

Just before the break, fresh boss Paolo Zanetti lost his first game against former club Venezia, with Udinese going down 2-1 in a crucial battle at the bottom.

Now, desperately needing some success, Zanetti must meet Palladino for the seventh time in management - to date, the pair have three wins apiece.

Unfortunately for fans of the Friulani, recent history is not on their side: they have won none of the last five meetings with Bologna, failing to even score in each of the last three.

Though Bologna will be without injured trio Jay Enem, Juan Miranda and Emil Holm, left-winger Nicolo Cambiaghi has resumed training after leaving Italy's UEFA Nations League camp.

Having impressed in the Azzurri's win over France, Cambiaghi has overcome a minor ankle problem and should start alongside Federico Bernadeschi in the final third.

The latter has previously scored four goals against Udinese, finding the net as a substitute in both of the last two meetings.

Bernardeschi and Samuel Mbangula - who recently hit a hat-trick at San Siro - are the hosts' joint-top Serie A scorers with three goals each; Jurgen Ekkelenkamp has netted three times for Udinese.

The visitors must travel without Nicolo Bertola, who has suffered a thigh injury in training and joins Idrissa Gueye on the sidelines.

In better news for Zanetti, David Alaba could return from his latest layoff, while Nicolo Zaniolo is available after withdrawing from the Italy squad for personal reasons.

Set to support Keinan Davis up front, Zaniolo has played eight league games against Bologna without ever scoring.

Bologna possible starting lineup:.

Skorupski; Darmian, Casale, Theate; Zortea, Ferguson, Pobega, Alhassane; Bernardeschi, Cambiaghi; Odgaard.

Udinese possible starting lineup:.

Okoye; Abankwah, Palma, Solet; Vojvoda, Karlstrom, Piotrowski, Kamara; Zaniolo, Ekkelenkamp; Davis.

Bologna may be in fine form but they tend to falter on home turf, while Udinese are struggling to pick up points anywhere.

Only Sassuolo have conceded more goals than the Friulani, and the Rossoblu have kept just a single clean sheet, so a score-draw could be on the cards.
